messages:
elaine: Heads-up — p95 token-service latency up ~40% on long-context hosts (~6k-10k tokens). I drilled into the runtime and it points at the kv eviction / reclaim path. Spike lines up with deploy abcde7 that increased evicter.batch_size to 64.

sam: Which metric shows the jump? p50/p95/p99? which cluster?

elaine: p50 ~ stable, p95 from 28ms -> 40ms, p99 saw the worst. Seen on us-west-2-dedicated pool (3 hosts). Happened right after rollout at 03:12 UTC.

jorge: I ran a quick perf sampling on one repro host. Flamegraph shows a big wedge in reclaim_scan and in slab_reinsert_hotpath. Looks like we do more work per-eviction when batch_size is bigger.

maria: We changed a related PR touching kv reinsert ordering earlier this week (diff: abcde7). Could be an interaction: larger batches + reinsert order causes more tombstone churn and fragmentation.

elaine: Here's the minimal config snippet I'm testing locally:
```
# evicter config
evicter.batch_size = 64
evicter.policy = "fifo"  # default on these hosts
reinsert.merge_tombstones = true
```
I toggled policy -> lru and p95 improved by ~8% locally but not resolved.

perf-bot: perf-run 6154321234 finished: flamegraph -> https://ci.redwood/p/runs/6154321234/flame.html (sampling 30s, symbols on)

sam: If LRU helps a bit, it suggests reuse pattern change. But 40% spike is big — maybe fragmentation or page faulting. Can you capture a heap profile + /proc/vmstat during a spike? Also enable kv telemetry for evicter step counts.

elaine: Dumped a heap profile and dmesg from host-3 during an incident window. Key excerpts: 
- vmstat.nr_inact_dirty +1200
- reclaim steals ~2-3ms more per loop
- repeated "evicter: reinsert chain len=512" logs
Link: https://artifacts/redwood/6154321000/host3-pprof.txt

jorge: From the profile: memcpy and page_copy show up in the hot path — suspect page churn and compaction overhead. Also saw more syscalls to madvise/MREMAP when big batches run.

infra-bot: Noted: host-3 had concurrent kernel OOM-kernel-reclaim events suppressed (no OOM kill). No disk IO spikes.

maria: Two hypotheses: (1) Larger batch_size leads to longer eviction windows, increasing chance of reinsert ordering creating fragmentation and longer reclaims. (2) Some recent matmul kernel change altered memory layout (model kernel's scratch allocator) increasing cache entry size and making evicter do more page ops.

sam: Agreed. Quick experiment plan:
- rollback evicter.batch_size to 16 on a canary host
- toggle policy fifo <-> lru on another host
- add a short-circuit to avoid full reinsert merge when chain > 256 (temporary)
- collect p95/p99 and pmap stats

elaine: Rolling batch_size back on canary now. Will run 30m. Also enabling lightweight kv telemetry (evict.count, reinsert.len histogram).

perf-bot: Canary rollout started for host: us-west-2-dedicated-1 at 6154321300.

jorge: I also instrumented the runtime to emit an event when eviction touches >1 page boundary (to detect fragmentation). Patch: https://git.redwood/r/evicter/+/pr/672

elaine: Canary p95 dropped from 40ms -> 30ms after batch_size=16. p99 still elevated but trending. eviction.count decreased ~45%. Fragmentation events still present but lower frequency.

maria: Good signal. Next: test the reinsert.shortcircuit for chain>256 and see if that prevents worst-case page churn. If it helps, we can tune policy heuristics.

sam: Also let's add a perf regression alert: if evicter.reinsert.len 99p > 300 for >5m then page_churn pager. Hook to runbook.

elaine: Will add alert and follow-up docs. Quick notes for postmortem:
- Root cause likely interaction between evicter.batch_size increase and reinsert ordering -> fragmentation and page-boundary work.
- Mitigation: rollback batch_size, short-circuit long reinserts, add LRU fallback for high reuse workloads.

perf-bot: perf-run 6154321400 scheduled for re-run with batch_size=16 and reinsert.shortcircuit enabled.

maria: Assigning follow-ups: @sam to add alert and runbook, @jorge to land lightweight fragmentation metric, @elaine to coordinate canary rollback and postmortem draft.

elaine: Thanks — I'll collect the traces and start the postmortem draft after the 2h observation window. :thumbsup:
